summary: The Fed is in an active hiking cycle with rates at 3.75-4.00% and markets pricing an 85% chance of a December hike, inflation remains elevated at 3.7% YoY, and S&P 500 trailing P/E around 29-30 is well above its long-run average — combined with a market-moving payrolls report this Friday and CPI next Tuesday, caution is warranted.
key_factors: Fed hiked in September, held in October (10-2 vote with two hawkish dissenters), December hike at ~85% probability — rates headed to 4.00-4.25%
September 2026 CPI: +3.7% YoY, up from +3.4% — inflation is re-accelerating, well above the Fed's 2% target
S&P 500 trailing P/E ~29-30 (August 2026 reading), forward P/E ~21-22x; both well above long-run averages of 16-19 and 18-19 respectively
October Nonfarm Payrolls release THIS FRIDAY November 6 at 8:30am ET — market-moving; recent payrolls have been soft (September +29K vs 90K forecast)
October CPI release NEXT TUESDAY November 10 at 8:30am ET — another market-moving event arriving soon
SPY is ABOVE its 200-day SMA (767.45 vs 729.89, +5.2%) — the technical trend is an uptrend, partially offsetting caution
All thesis candidates trading 35-50% above our fair-value estimates, confirming the broad market is expensive on our measures
events: Nonfarm Payrolls (Oct 2026): Friday Nov 6, 8:30am ET — market-moving
CPI Inflation Report (Oct 2026): Tuesday Nov 10, 8:30am ET — market-moving
FOMC Minutes (Oct 27-28 meeting): Wednesday Nov 18, 2:00pm ET
Next FOMC rate decision: Wednesday Dec 9, 2026
rates: rising — fed funds target 3.75-4.00% as of Oct 28; December hike (~4.00-4.25%) priced at ~85%
inflation: elevated — Sep 2026 CPI +3.7% YoY, re-accelerating from +3.4% in August
market_trend_note: SPY above 200-day SMA is a bullish technical signal, but it does not override the fundamental backdrop of elevated rates, hot inflation, and stretched valuations
note: Futures data for today (Nov 4) was not available from the web search; the cautious posture is based on the confirmed rate environment, inflation trajectory, valuation measures, and event calendar. Confidence is medium rather than high because one piece of the picture (intraday futures direction) is missing.

sector_notes.technology: Highest-multiple sector; most exposed to rate rises and re-rating risk. AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL all 35-50% above our fair values.
sector_notes.financials: Banks benefit from higher net interest margins in a rising-rate environment, but credit risk rises if the economy slows. V still 39% above fair value.
sector_notes.consumer_discretionary: MCD is the closest to fair value at -16.5% margin of safety, but conviction is only 3 — still not actionable without a conviction upgrade.
sector_notes.consumer_staples: Defensive names (KO, PEP, PG, WMT) have no thesis yet. COST is 47% above our fair value.
sector_notes.health_care: No theses built. Worth prioritising for bench expansion.
sector_notes.industrials: No theses built. Railroad names (UNP, CSX) worth researching — tend to be less rate-sensitive on a moat basis.
